text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) say their plans for tax reform are intended to reduce burden on workers and families.
- Proescutors investigate Frankfurt police chief over allegations he abused privileges of office.
- Foreign companies avoiding Germany as an industrial location. Foreign direct investment hits record low of 1.1 billion marks.
- Swiss chemical giant Roche buys Germany's Boehringer Mannheim.
- SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine threatens to reject the so-called "Maastricht II" treaty on European integration if it does not contain plans for active employment policy.
- SPD proposals bring moevment into row over tax reform.
- Churches warn of dangers of right-wing extremism following arson attack on a Luebeck church.
- SPD tax plans make agreement with government more likely.
- Provisional west German inflation rises to 1.5 percent in May.
- Imports into Germany cheaper in April, above all due to lower oil price.
- Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), offers SPD new talks on tax reform.
- Kohl backs Finance Minister Waigel in row with Free Democrat (FDP) coalition partners over how to plug budget shortfalls.
- German doctors say health funds must cut back on operations and services they are prepared to pay for.
